newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl calls for 25 billion mark investment drive.
newsitem.headline: Kohl calls for 25 billion mark investment drive.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl has said he wants to pump 25 billion marks, mostly in cheap state-backed credits, into Germany's stricken construction sector.
According to the text of a speech Kohl gave on Wednesday in Munich, his coalition cabinet will decide on the investment drive when it meets next week.
"In the short term we want to mobilise extra building investment and thereby stabilise the jobs-intensive construction sector," Kohl said.

Kohl said 20 billion marks in credits would be provided by development agency the Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau and the Deutsche Ausgleichsbank, and a further five billion will come from accelerating public infrastructure investment.

Germany has an estimated 400,000 unemployed building workers. Construction output slumped by a quarter in January, and idled building workers were largely to blame for the winter surge in unemployment to a post-war record of 4.7 million.

The investments, already signalled by Finance Minister Theo Waigel last month, would be mainly off-budget items and would thus have no impact on Germany's ability to meet borrowing requirements required to join European monetary union (EMU).
"Overall, we want parts of these projects to create jobs in 1997," Kohl said.
"The necessary consolidation efforts in the budget will not be affected by the job-creating investment programme -- they must be continued independently."

Despite doubts from leading economists and several senior central bankers that Germany would meet the Maastricht deficit target of three percent of GDP this year, Kohl has repeatedly said that Bonn would qualify and join monetary union on time.
